plans.objective: Verify bit-exact output equality against an independently computed floor-modulo permutation for a small valid invocation with positive shifts.
plans.observation: For every 0 <= x < W and 0 <= y < H, read the 4 bytes at odata[y*P + x] and the 4 bytes at source[floor_mod(y + shiftY, H)*W + floor_mod(x + shiftX, W)], where floor_mod(a, n) = a - n*floor(a/n) and source is the exact source buffer supplied to the candidate.
plans.pass_condition: For every logical coordinate (x, y), the 4 bytes at odata[y*P + x] are bit-for-bit identical (host-side memcmp == 0) to the 4 bytes at source[floor_mod(y + shiftY, H)*W + floor_mod(x + shiftX, W)]. Equality is exact binary32 bit-pattern equality with no numeric tolerance; any interpolation, rounding, scaling, or conversion that changes a single bit fails.
plans.setup: Set W=5, H=4, P=5, shiftX=2, shiftY=3. Allocate a contiguous source buffer of W*H binary32 elements and fill source[r*W+c] with 20 distinct, known binary32 bit patterns (include -0.0f, several finite values, and at least one NaN payload); record the exact bit pattern at each index. Allocate a separate output buffer with H rows and P elements per row, zero-initialize it, and pass it to the candidate as odata. Explicitly pass the exact filled source buffer to the candidate as its source input for this invocation: either as a direct source pointer/array/tensor argument, or by binding a required source/resource/texture handle to this exact buffer and passing that handle (as the original CUDA entry point does with its cudaTextureObject_t parameter at lines 225-226). Invoke the candidate shiftPitchLinear entry point once with the source input and parameters (odata, pitch=P, width=W, height=H, shiftX, shiftY), using a launch configuration that covers exactly the logical W-by-H output region, then read the output buffer back to the host.

plans.objective: Verify that two inverse shifts are exact inverses: applying shift (a,b) followed by shift (-a,-b) reproduces the original input bit-for-bit, a necessary property of the exact floor-modulo permutation.
plans.observation: For every 0 <= x < W and 0 <= y < H, read the 4 bytes at output2[y*P + x] and the 4 bytes at the original source[y*W + x].
plans.pass_condition: For all 12 logical coordinates, output2[y*P + x] is bit-for-bit identical to source[y*W + x]. This holds only if each invocation performs the exact floor-modulo permutation so shiftB exactly inverts shiftA; any interpolation, rounding, scaling, or C-style remainder behavior would leave at least one differing bit pattern.
plans.setup: Set W=4, H=3, P=5, shiftA=(2,-1), shiftB=(-2,1). Fill a contiguous source buffer of W*H binary32 elements with 12 distinct, known bit patterns (include -0.0f and at least one NaN payload). Allocate output1 and output2 buffers, each with H rows and P elements per row, zero-initialize both. For the first invocation, explicitly supply the exact filled source buffer to the candidate as its source input (a direct source pointer/array/tensor argument, or a required source/resource/texture handle bound to this exact buffer) and pass output1 as odata. Invoke the candidate with the source input, shiftA, and parameters (odata, P, W, H, shiftX, shiftY). Copy only the logical W-by-H region of output1 into a second contiguous source buffer (discarding padding). For the second invocation, explicitly supply this second source buffer to the candidate as its source input and pass output2 as odata, then invoke with shiftB. Use a launch configuration that covers exactly the logical W-by-H output region in each invocation, then read output2 back to the host.

plans.objective: Confirm that the migrated implementation of shiftPitchLinear derives each output element's source coordinate using integer floor-modulo arithmetic and performs a direct binary32 copy, rather than normalized-coordinate texture sampling with interpolation or numeric conversion.
plans.observation: Record the formulas used to compute the source row and source column, any operations applied to the loaded value, and the expression that stores the value to odata[y*P + x].
plans.pass_condition: The code computes srcRow = floor_mod(y + shiftY, H) and srcCol = floor_mod(x + shiftX, W) using integer arithmetic equivalent to mathematical floor modulo (a - n*floor(a/n)) for all representable operands, loads the exact binary32 element from source[srcRow*W + srcCol] (or an equivalent row-major address into the logical W-by-H source region), and writes that same binary32 value to odata[y*P + x] with no interpolation, filtering, scaling, rounding, or numeric type conversion in the load-to-store path.
plans.setup: Obtain the migrated Ascend-C source for the shiftPitchLinear operator. Locate the kernel/operator body that computes the value stored at odata[y*P + x] for each logical output coordinate (x, y), including how the source input is read and how the source row and source column are derived from x, y, shiftX, shiftY, W, and H.

plans.objective: Verify exact floor-modulo wrap behavior for negative shifts and boundary coordinates, cases where a C-style remainder implementation would select a different source element.
plans.observation: For every 0 <= x < 3 and 0 <= y < 3, read the 4 bytes at odata[y*P + x] and the 4 bytes at source[floor_mod(y + shiftY, 3)*3 + floor_mod(x + shiftX, 3)], where floor_mod(a, n) = a - n*floor(a/n).
plans.pass_condition: All 9 output elements are bit-for-bit equal to the source element at the floor_mod indices. In particular, for x=0 and y=0 the output must equal source[floor_mod(-2,3)*3 + floor_mod(-1,3)] = source[1*3 + 2] = source[5], and for x=2 and y=2 it must equal source[floor_mod(0,3)*3 + floor_mod(1,3)] = source[0*3 + 1] = source[1]; a C remainder expression would produce a negative index and fail these boundaries.
plans.setup: Set W=3, H=3, P=4, shiftX=-1, shiftY=-2. Fill a contiguous source buffer of 9 binary32 elements with 9 distinct, known bit patterns including -0.0f and one NaN payload so bitwise equality is observable. Allocate a separate output buffer with H rows and P elements per row (12 elements), zero-initialize it, and pass it to the candidate as odata. Explicitly pass the exact filled source buffer to the candidate as its source input: either as a direct source pointer/array/tensor argument, or by binding a required source/resource/texture handle to this exact buffer and passing that handle (as the original CUDA entry point does with its cudaTextureObject_t parameter). Invoke the candidate shiftPitchLinear entry point once with the source input and parameters (odata, P, W, H, shiftX, shiftY), using a launch configuration that covers exactly the logical W-by-H output region, then read the output buffer back to the host.
